title: The Mali Empire and Mansa Musa: gold, salt and the 1324 pilgrimage
examples: Why was the Mali Empire so rich?
How do we know about medieval Mali?

nodes.label: Gold fields
nodes.ask: Why was the Mali Empire so rich?

explain.say: In 1324 a West African king arrived in Cairo on his way to Mecca with a huge caravan and so much gold that, according to the Cairo writer al-Umari, its value there stayed low for years. He was Mansa Musa, ruler of Mali. Look at the network: where did all that gold come from?

draw.text: The Mali Empire and Mansa Musa: gold, salt and the 1324 pilgrimage

nodes.label: Gold fields
nodes.ask: Why was the Mali Empire so rich?

explain.say: Start at the gold fields in the bottom corner, in the upper Senegal and Niger valleys. Mali's rulers controlled the trade. Gold went north across the Sahara, and salt came south from mines at Taghaza, because salt was precious in the hot south. Why would salt be worth so much?

nodes.label: Gold fields
nodes.ask: Why was the Mali Empire so rich?

explain.say: Follow Musa's pilgrimage on the map, from Timbuktu across the Sahara to Cairo and Mecca. He was a Muslim ruler of a kingdom where many also kept older beliefs. He came home with scholars and an architect, and a great mosque rose in Timbuktu, the Djinguereber. Why would a king bring scholars home?

The timeline shows the empire's story. It began around 1235 with Sunjata Keita, still celebrated by griots. The traveller Ibn Battuta visited in 1352 and admired its safety and justice, while criticising some customs. The Catalan Atlas of 1375 shows Mali's ruler holding gold, so Europeans knew of Mali. When did Mali's power fade?

explain.say: How do we know Mali's history? See the comparison: Arabic writers saw it from outside, griots from within. Historians use both, plus archaeology. Musa is often called the richest person ever, but his wealth cannot really be measured. Superb work. Challenge: give one strength and one weakness of each kind of source.

faq.a: The ruler of the Mali Empire, about 1312 to 1337. He is famous for his 1324 pilgrimage to Mecca via Cairo, where his gifts of gold amazed observers, and for building mosques and supporting scholarship in Timbuktu.
asks: Who was the mansa of Mali?
Was Mansa Musa the richest man ever?

faq.q: Why was the Mali Empire so rich?
faq.a: It controlled gold-producing regions and the trade routes linking them to the trans-Saharan caravans, taxing gold, salt, copper and other goods as they moved between West Africa and North Africa.
asks: Where did Mali's gold come from?

faq.q: What happened when Mansa Musa visited Cairo?
faq.a: During his 1324 pilgrimage he spent and gave away so much gold that, according to al-Umari, writing some years later, its value in Cairo fell and had not recovered over a decade afterwards.

faq.q: What did Ibn Battuta say about Mali?
faq.a: Visiting in 1352 to 1353, the Moroccan traveller praised Mali's security, its justice and its people's devotion to prayer, while disapproving of some local customs. His account is a vital outside source.

Timbuktu was a trading city where Saharan caravans met river trade on the Niger, and a centre of Islamic scholarship with mosques and libraries. Families there kept hundreds of thousands of manuscripts.

facts: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage passed through Cairo in 1324.
Ibn Battuta visited the Mali Empire in 1352 and 1353.
The Catalan Atlas of 1375 depicts the ruler of Mali holding a gold nugget.

quiz.say: What did Mali mainly send north across the Sahara?
quiz.show: Mali's main export across the Sahara was…
quiz.why: West African gold was the great prize of trans-Saharan trade.

wrong.1: Salt went the other way, from Saharan mines south to Mali.
wrong.2: Silk came from China and was not a Malian export.

quiz.say: Which kind of source tells Mali's story from the inside?
quiz.show: Which source gives an insider's view of Mali?
quiz.why: Griots, hereditary oral historians, preserve Mali's own tradition about Sunjata and his ancestors.

wrong.1: Al-Umari wrote in Cairo, as an outsider.
wrong.2: The Catalan Atlas was made in Majorca, by Europeans.
